themes_detail.label: Tree Emergency in East Flatbush
themes_detail.summary: Dead, dying, and damaged trees are surging THIS WEEK across East Flatbush—7 dead/dying tree complaints last week vs. 0.2 weekly average, and 6 damaged tree complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.5 weekly average—suggesting a potential storm, disease outbreak, or infrastructure failure affecting the neighborhood's canopy.
evidence: Dead/Dying Tree complaints: 7 last week vs. 0.2 weekly average (2700% spike, z-score 15.59)
Damaged Tree complaints: 6 THIS WEEK vs. 1.5 weekly average (300% spike, z-score 4.5)
Combined tree-related emergency: 13 complaints in past 7-10 days vs. ~1.7 baseline
reporting_angles: Interview Parks Dept. about disease, storm damage, or maintenance failures driving the spike
Document which blocks/neighborhoods are most affected and canvass residents for safety concerns
Investigate whether budget cuts to tree maintenance or delayed storm cleanup are contributing factors

themes_detail.label: Electrical System Failures Spiking
themes_detail.summary: Electrical complaints tripled THIS WEEK to 3 reports vs. 0.1 weekly average (2300% spike, z-score 8.69), signaling potential widespread wiring hazards, overloaded systems, or infrastructure degradation affecting buildings across the district.
evidence: Electrical complaints: 3 THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average (2300% spike, z-score 8.69)
Pattern suggests acute rather than chronic issue given extreme statistical deviation
Low baseline (0.1/week) makes this a true anomaly, not seasonal trend
reporting_angles: Request Con Edison incident reports for East Flatbush this week; investigate power surges or grid failures
File FOIL for DOB electrical violations filed in past 7 days; any correlation with new construction (319 permits filed)?
Contact Buildings Dept. about whether substandard wiring in older housing stock is being exposed by this week's demand spike

themes_detail.label: Street Sanitation Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street sweeping complaints exploded last week to 15 vs. 1.6 weekly average (823% spike, z-score 5.71), and residential waste complaints surged to 11 vs. 2.9 average (283% spike, z-score 6.97)—together signaling a municipal sanitation breakdown affecting both street cleanliness and building waste management.
evidence: Street Sweeping complaints: 15 last week vs. 1.6 weekly average (823% spike, z-score 5.71)
Residential Disposal complaints: 11 last week vs. 2.9 weekly average (283% spike, z-score 6.97)
Combined 26 sanitation complaints in one week vs. ~4.5 baseline suggests coordinated service failure
reporting_angles: Obtain DSNY schedules: are sweeping routes been cut or delayed? Interview district manager about staffing or equipment issues
Visit affected blocks; photograph uncleaned streets and overflowing waste to visualize scale
Cross-reference with CB budget requests: has East Flatbush repeatedly asked for more sanitation funding? Is this a breaking point?

themes_detail.label: Parking & Driveway Obstruction Epidemic
themes_detail.summary: Over the past 90 days, illegal parking (1,645 complaints) and blocked driveways (1,415 complaints) are the 2nd and 4th highest complaint categories, totaling 3,060 complaints—a structural parking shortage or enforcement failure affecting daily resident mobility and suggesting tension over scarce curb space.
evidence: Illegal Parking: 1,645 complaints over 90 days (2nd highest category)
Blocked Driveway: 1,415 complaints over 90 days (4th highest category)
Combined 3,060 complaints = ~34 per day, indicating systemic problem affecting many residents
reporting_angles: Analyze parking permit utilization vs. available spaces; interview DOT about enforcement presence and staffing
Profile residents with chronic blocked driveways; calculate economic impact of delayed access
Investigate whether new development (319 permits filed, 81 new buildings) has reduced available parking without adding spaces

themes_detail.label: Heat/Hot Water Emergency (90-day trend)
themes_detail.summary: Heat and hot water complaints dominate the district's 311 calls (4,911 over 90 days, far exceeding all other categories), reflecting a chronic housing crisis likely tied to aging building infrastructure, inadequate landlord maintenance, and winter vulnerability—though no THIS WEEK spike is evident, the sheer volume signals a systemic breakdown.
evidence: Heat/Hot Water: 4,911 complaints over 90 days (by far the highest category, 2.7x the 2nd highest)
Implies ~55 complaints per day of heating emergencies affecting families
Pattern suggests aging building stock and landlord non-compliance; not a recent spike but a chronic crisis
reporting_angles: Map heat complaint hotspots; identify which buildings/blocks have repeat violations and why
Interview HPD about enforcement: how many landlords face penalties vs. complaints filed?
Profile 2-3 families in unheated units; calculate health costs and explore whether gentrification pressures are contributing to landlord disinvestment
